title: Planning Performance Domain
coreMove: Planning performance is healthy when scope, schedule, budget, and resource signals stay current enough to guide choices across all eight PMBOK Guide domains.

exampleSpecs.domain: Planning Performance Domain signals after a scope change
exampleSpecs.audience: project managers who treat an approved schedule as stable after scope moves
exampleSpecs.stakes: the team may keep executing against a schedule that no longer matches scope, budget, or resources
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same wall plan appears before and after the scope change, with the contrast showing whether planning information stayed useful.

exampleSpecs.domain: Eight-domain system around the Planning Performance Domain
exampleSpecs.audience: PMO reviewers checking whether planning has become isolated from other domains
exampleSpecs.stakes: a file can look complete while stakeholder, delivery, measurement, and uncertainty effects remain disconnected
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The reviewer studies records and finds the detail that proves Planning Performance Domain is not being read with the other seven domains.

exampleSpecs.audience: workstream leads who feel pressure to keep a plan looking settled
exampleSpecs.stakes: a plan can stay polished while budget and resources quietly contradict schedule promises
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist works through the wrong turns internally before choosing how to read scope, schedule, budget, and resources together.

exampleSpecs.domain: Planning Performance Domain interaction with other PMBOK Guide domains
exampleSpecs.audience: planning leads allocating scarce review time before work begins
exampleSpecs.stakes: attention spent on artifact cleanup may leave domain interactions invisible
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before action begins, the protagonist allocates scarce attention across planning signals and the eight-domain map.

exampleSpecs.audience: project leads facing two damaging planning choices
exampleSpecs.stakes: protecting one signal may damage value, while reopening another may damage trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist faces one genuine two-bad-options decision about scope and schedule.

exampleSpecs.domain: Planning Performance Domain dialogue across the eight-domain system
exampleSpecs.audience: teams learning to talk about planning as current coordination
exampleSpecs.stakes: a plan review can become artifact checking instead of domain interaction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two named people talk, and the lesson emerges through their exchange rather than a summary.
